web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Reading the Tape: Stage 2 Uptrend vs. Downtrend Regime & Failed Asymmetry
question: What does the 1W/1D/4H tape show across the Nov 20 verified close ($1,069.43) and Nov 23 snapshot ($1,052.21), and why does the $994.71–$1,066.83 support zone still fail our 1.50:1 hurdle?

epigraph.quote: A strong Stage 2 chart cannot rescue a trade when the structural stop sits too far below support.
epigraph.author: Stage Analysis Desk Principle

web_blocks.title: Stage 2 Uptrend Inside a Confirmed Market Downtrend

web_blocks.html: The broader U.S. market sits in a confirmed Downtrend. Only 38.8% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average (46.9% above the 200-day), and the index logged 10 distribution days in 25 sessions [24]. Against that weak backdrop, McKesson remained a Stage 2 Markup leader (+32.04% 63-day relative strength and +22.52% 28-day RS) [24]. Shares closed at $1,069.43 on November 20, 2026 (+0.68% 1D, -3.03% 1W, +22.39% 3M) before easing to $1,052.21 (-1.64%) on the November 23 TradingView snapshot [24].

We override that screen to REJECTED (VALUATION) because fundamental fair value ($1,160.00) against the $865.85 invalidation stop yields only 0.45:1 R:R at $1,069.43 and 1.28:1 at the $994.71 zone low [24].

web_blocks.title: Why Even the $994.71 Support Zone Fails the 1.50:1 Hurdle (and Options Are Declined)

web_blocks.html: At $1,069.43 against our $865.85 structural stop (ratcheted up from prior $857.69), downside risk is $203.58 per share while upside to our $1,160.00 DCF Base is $90.57—a 0.45:1 ratio (0.51:1 to Finviz's $1,173.21) [24, 25]. Even if MCK pulls back to the bottom of the snapshot support band ($994.71), upside is $165.29 against $128.86 of stop risk, yielding 1.28:1—below our mandatory 1.50:1 gate [24].

Options also fail the risk-sizing test. The batch screen flagged a 1x 2027-09-17 $960 LEAPS Call (298 DTE, 0.71 delta) at $183.65/sh ($18,365.00 max loss). On our $75,110.60 portfolio net worth and $2,540.35 US cash balance, one contract consumes 2,445.1 bps (24.45% of NAV) and 7.23x available cash. We therefore mark options as NO_OPTIONS_EDGE / DECLINED.

Volume behavior confirms institutional digestion rather than fresh accumulation. On the November 20 close ($1,069.43), volume ran at 869,500 shares (1.22x 20-day average), whereas the November 23 dip to $1,052.21 occurred on lighter 237,597-share volume (0.34x 30-day average) [24]. Daily 14-day ATR sits at $25.52–$25.95 (~2.4% of price) [24]. In a Downtrend regime with 38.8% S&P 500 breadth above the 50-day SMA, a routine 3.5-to-4.0 ATR shakeout ($90–$104) pulls MCK directly into the $965–$979 zone near the rising 50-day SMA ($974.32–$977.15) [24].

Our structural stop-loss is ratcheted upward from $857.69 to $865.85 per the snapshot invalidation rule, sitting just below the rising 30-week SMA ($878.61) and 200-day SMA ($879.78–$880.30) [24]. Because that stop cannot be tightened inside normal weekly noise without inviting whipsaw, the only way to achieve 1.50:1 reward-to-risk toward our $1,160.00 Base target is an entry below $980.00 (specifically $980.00 yields ($1,160 - $980) / ($980 - $865.85) = 1.58:1). Above $980.00—including the entire $994.71–$1,066.83 snapshot support band—the trade fails our hurdle.

Cross-checking pivot levels reinforces the same caution. Near-term resistance sits at Pivot R1 ($1,056.12) and the 52-week high ($1,121.50), while initial daily support sits at the 20-day SMA ($1,045.53–$1,048.51) and 4H 50-SMA ($1,040.06) [24]. Deeper structural support sits at the 20-day swing low ($954.05), Pivot S1 ($907.19), and the primary Stage 2 floor at the 30-week SMA ($878.61) and 200-day SMA ($880.30) [24].

book_paragraphs: A healthy chart does not automatically make a healthy investment. Across weekly, daily, and four-hour timeframes, McKesson remains in a Stage 2 Markup [24]. It outperformed the S&P 500 by +32.04% over 63 trading days even while market breadth sank to 38.8% above the 50-day moving average with 10 distribution days [24]. Shares closed at $1,069.43 on November 20 before dipping to $1,052.21 in the November 23 snapshot [24].

Yet when we pair the tape with our revised $1,160.00 DCF Base fair value and the upward-ratcheted $865.85 invalidation stop, the math breaks [24]. Buying at $1,069.43 risks $203.58 for $90.57 of upside—just 0.45-to-1. Even waiting for the $994.71 lower edge of the snapshot support zone risks $128.86 for $165.29 of upside, or 1.28-to-1, failing our 1.50-to-1 minimum threshold [24].

Meanwhile, the suggested 1x 2027-09-17 $960 LEAPS Call ($18,365 max loss) would tie up 24.45% of our $75,110.60 NAV—7.23x our $2,540.35 cash balance—on an over-extended underlying. Discipline requires declining both the equity and the LEAPS.

Technical analysis serves one purpose in our process: keeping us out of bad risk-reward setups even when a business looks strong. On the chart, McKesson sits in a Stage 2 Markup [24]. It trades roughly 20% above its rising 30-week SMA ($878.61) and 21% above its 200-day SMA ($880.30), with +32.04% 63-day relative strength against the S&P 500 [24].

However, short-term momentum is cooling inside a hostile market tape. Only 38.8% of S&P 500 stocks hold above their 50-day moving average, and the index has logged 10 distribution days in 25 sessions [24]. On the 4-hour chart, McKesson's RSI has dropped to 45.04 below its 4H 20-EMA ($1,071.11) with no upward turn yet [24]. On the daily chart, 14-day ATR is $25.95, meaning a normal three-to-four-ATR pullback in a Downtrend removes $78 to $104 per share [24].

Now check the stop-loss math. Our upward-ratcheted structural stop sits at $865.85 (above the prior $857.69 stop), safely tucked beneath the 30-week and 200-day moving averages [24]. If you buy at $1,069.43 for a $1,160.00 Base target, you risk $203.58 to make $90.57—a 0.45:1 ratio. Even if you wait patiently for $994.71, you risk $128.86 to make $165.29—a 1.28:1 ratio that still falls short of 1.50:1. Only a drop below $980.00 restores 1.50:1 math.

We also audited the suggested 1x 2027-09-17 $960 LEAPS Call ($183.65 per share, 298 DTE, 0.71 delta) [24]. Paying $18,365.00 for one contract would consume 2,445.1 bps (24.45%) of our $75,110.60 portfolio net worth and 7.23 times our $2,540.35 US cash balance. Concentrating a quarter of the entire portfolio into one over-valued equity's option violates every risk-budget rule, so we decline the trade.

Tape reading is often misunderstood as chart-gazing, but at an institutional desk it is really about measuring supply, demand, and exit distance. When the S&P 500 enters a Downtrend with only 38.8% of constituents above their 50-day moving average and 10 distribution days in 25 sessions, even the strongest Stage 2 leaders face air pockets [24]. Portfolio managers raise cash by trimming their biggest winners—stocks like McKesson that rallied +39.48% over six months [24].

We can already see that digestion starting on the shorter timeframes. Between the November 20 close ($1,069.43) and the November 23 snapshot ($1,052.21), daily RSI(14) cooled from 60.34 to 54.62, while weekly RSI eased to 67.71 [24]. On the 4-hour chart, RSI dropped to 45.04 below the 4H 20-EMA ($1,071.11), and our intraday turn indicator remained false [24]. A routine three-to-four-ATR pullback in this regime—roughly $78 to $104 per share—naturally targets the $965 to $979 region around the rising 50-day SMA ($974.32–$977.15) [24].

Yet even if McKesson pulls back to the bottom of the snapshot support band at $994.71, our valuation ceiling prevents a buy signal. Why? Because the structural invalidation stop sits at $865.85 (ratcheted upward from the prior $857.69 stop), just beneath the rising 30-week SMA ($878.61) and 200-day SMA ($880.30) [24]. Risking $128.86 from $994.71 to $865.85 for $165.29 of upside to $1,160.00 yields 1.28:1—still short of our 1.50:1 minimum.

The options overlay confirms this lack of edge. While implied volatility (34.1%) is fair against 20-day realized volatility (31.9%), buying 1x 2027-09-17 $960 LEAPS Call requires $18,365.00 upfront [24]. Against a $75,110.60 portfolio and $2,540.35 of US cash, that single contract equals 24.45% of total net worth and 7.23x available cash. Declining the LEAPS as NO_OPTIONS_EDGE / DECLINED protects liquidity.

When a stock sits in a Stage 2 Markup while the broader index sits in a Downtrend, traders often assume relative strength makes the stock immune to pullbacks. History teaches the opposite. In a market Downtrend with 38.8% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day moving average and 10 distribution days in 25 sessions, institutional desks routinely harvest gains from their best performers to meet redemptions or de-risk books [24].

Look at the exact multi-timeframe footprints we captured between November 20 and November 23, 2026 [24]. On November 20, McKesson closed at $1,069.43, still +9.76% above its 50-day SMA ($974.32) and +21.56% above its 200-day SMA ($879.78), with daily RSI(14) at 60.34 and 14-day ATR at $25.95 [24]. By the November 23 snapshot, shares had eased to $1,052.21 (-1.64%), pulling daily RSI down to 54.62 and weekly RSI to 67.71 [24].

On the 4-hour chart, the cooling is even clearer. Four-hour RSI dropped to 45.04, sitting below the 4-hour 20-EMA ($1,071.11) with no upward turn yet [24]. Meanwhile, the nearest major daily support shelf sits at the rising 50-day SMA ($974.32–$977.15) and the 20-day swing low ($954.05), while the primary Stage 2 floor rests at the 30-week SMA ($878.61) and 200-day SMA ($880.30) [24].

This is where our upward-only stop ratchet meets valuation reality. Because the structural stop-loss is set at $865.85 (above the prior $857.69 stop), any entry above $980.00 fails to deliver 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk toward our $1,160.00 Base target. At $1,069.43, R:R is 0.45:1; at the $994.71 support zone low, R:R is 1.28:1 [24]. Even the 1x 2027-09-17 $960 LEAPS Call ($18,365 max loss) would consume 24.45% of our $75,110.60 NAV—7.23x our $2,540.35 US cash—so we decline it as NO_OPTIONS_EDGE.

Practically speaking, what would change our technical and valuation verdict? Two paths exist. On the price path, a deeper Downtrend flush below $980.00—toward the 20-day swing low ($954.05) or Pivot S1 ($907.19)—combined with a 4H momentum reversal would restore >=1.50:1 reward-to-risk against our $865.85 stop [24].

On the fundamental path, clean Wellverse Form 10 disclosures, smooth CEO transition execution, and faster-than-expected PMG synergies that lift Base fair value above $1,250.00 would also reopen the case [3, 13]. Until one of those two events occurs, standing aside in 100% cash and declining the $18,365 LEAPS call is the only disciplined move.

In sum, the chart and the valuation tell two halves of the same story. Weekly and daily trends remain constructive in Stage 2, yet 4-hour momentum has cooled to RSI 45.04 inside an S&P 500 Downtrend (38.8% breadth above 50DMA, 10 distribution days) [24]. Because the upward-ratcheted $865.85 stop sits 12.95% below the $994.71 support zone low, even a textbook pullback to $994.71 delivers just 1.28:1 reward-to-risk toward $1,160.00—leaving no valid equity or LEAPS entry.

Respecting the $865.85 invalidation stop and declining the $18,365 LEAPS call (24.45% of NAV) keeps portfolio risk-heat bounded during an S&P 500 Downtrend. Discipline before entry prevents forced exits later.

By anchoring every decision to verified session closes ($1,069.43 on November 20 and $1,052.21 on November 23) and refusing to stretch our 1.50:1 reward-to-risk hurdle, we ensure that chart strength never overrides valuation discipline.
